title: Bronson's reed section: Albert Walters, Buford Boswell and Lester's tenor
summary: After a phone-call pause, Phillips recalls Lester left his Buescher horns with his father, Bronson bought the tenor, and Boswell was a good reader.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: That's when he was playing with his father?
Yeah, and a Buesher baritone. Yeah, everything he had was Buesher. That's what he had. He left all that. Then Bronson went down to the music store and got him a tenor. We sent and go this...
I was talking about Albert Walters...
Before the telephone call, you were talking about Albert Walters, and you were talking about Lester getting that Pan-American tenor that Bronson bought for him.
Yeah, he got that, then Bronson had those three guys. Buford was a good reader and played pretty good solos too in the band.
